object_types.name: Incident
object_types.definition: An event that has been declared or is in triage, tracked from origin through resolution.

object_types.name: IncidentNumber
object_types.definition: Unique identifier for an incident, format INC- followed by a sequence, never reused.

source_references.excerpt: Incident number. INC-, then a sequence. ... Unique. And we never delete incidents

object_types.name: Alert
object_types.definition: A notification from the monitoring platform (or a manual alert raised by an engineer) that can be linked to an incident.

source_references.excerpt: Monitoring fires an alert, or a customer tells us.

object_types.name: AlertId

object_types.name: Ticket
object_types.definition: A customer support ticket that can be linked to an incident as its origin.

object_types.name: Severity
object_types.definition: Blast radius / technical impact classification of an incident, from SEV1 (everyone down) to SEV4 (cosmetic, one region).

source_references.excerpt: SEV1 through SEV4. It's about blast radius and technical impact.

object_types.name: Priority
object_types.definition: Customer urgency classification of an incident, from P1 to P4, independent of severity.

source_references.excerpt: And priority is P1 through P4.
Priority is about customer urgency.

object_types.name: IncidentState
object_types.definition: The current lifecycle state of an incident.

object_types.name: Person

ambiguities.description: Commander mandatory/optional depends on incident state (mandatory when declared, none in triage), which is a conditional/exclusive rule not fully expressible as a simple mandatory constraint tied only to the state value. Should the model include a subset/conditional constraint linking IncidentState='declared' (or later) to presence of a commander, and absence when state='triage'?

source_references.excerpt: A commander is assigned when it's declared. If it turns out to be nothing, it gets closed from triage having never had one. ... Declared incidents have exactly one commander. Triage incidents have none.

ambiguities.description: Severity and Priority change over time (severity revised, presumably priority too), and history is kept 'in the timeline as events' but the incident record only carries the current value. Should a separate Timeline/Event entity be modeled to capture historical severity/priority changes, or is current-state-only modeling sufficient for this exercise?

source_references.excerpt: Severity gets revised as we understand the blast radius. That's normal and expected. ... In the timeline, as events. The incident record carries the current severity.

ambiguities.description: The term 'owner' is overloaded: 'service owner' (a team, standing assignment) versus 'incident commander' (a person, temporary role) versus general channel usage. This is captured as two separate fact types (Team owns Service, Incident is commanded by Person), but stakeholders explicitly flagged genuine ambiguity in casual usage -- worth confirming no third 'owner' concept exists.

source_references.excerpt: Now -- the other 'owner.' ... 'who owns this?' means either. It's genuinely ambiguous every single time.

ambiguities.description: Severity vs Priority are described as 'independent' but Owen initially claimed correlation ('A P1 is always a SEV1') which Nadia refuted with counterexamples. No constraint should link them, but it's worth confirming stakeholders agree there is truly zero correlation rule to encode (not even a soft/default one).

source_references.excerpt: A P1 is always a SEV1. ... That is not true. ... You'd have lost.

ambiguities.description: A 'monitoring' status was raised by Owen as something people treat as a state between mitigated and resolved, but explicitly excluded from the model since it's not in the system dropdown. Confirm this exclusion is correct and won't need to be added later as an actual system state.

source_references.excerpt: There's also 'monitoring,' which sits between mitigated and resolved. ... If it's not in the system I'm not modelling it. Five states.

ambiguities.description: Classification of incidents later found to be caused by customer misconfiguration (whether to reclassify, exclude from reliability metrics, or leave as-is) is explicitly parked/undecided pending a decision from Ravi. No 'cause classification' concept is modeled, per explicit agreement, but this is a known gap that will require a future model update.

source_references.excerpt: Is there a decision here today? ... No, and it's above all three of us. ... Whether an incident later found to be caused by customer misconfiguration should be reclassified, excluded from reliability metrics, or left as-is, is undecided.

ambiguities.description: Person identification: reference_mode 'person_name' is inferred but the transcript only says the commander is 'one person, named' without specifying a formal identifier scheme (e.g., employee ID, username). Person names may not be unique in a real organization; confirm whether a different identifier (e.g., employee ID) should be used instead.

source_references.excerpt: The incident commander. One person, named, and it's a role for the duration, not a job title.

ambiguities.description: Team identification: reference_mode 'team_name' is inferred by analogy with Service naming, but the transcript never explicitly states team names are unique or how teams are identified. Confirm the actual identification scheme for Team.

source_references.excerpt: A team. Services are owned by teams. People move.

ambiguities.description: The ring constraint on Incident-is-duplicate-of-Incident: the group agrees chains 'shouldn't' happen and the primary should not itself be a duplicate, but also explicitly states this rule 'is not enforced' today in the actual system. Should the model capture this as a hard constraint (as intended) or note it as an aspirational/unenforced rule only?

source_references.excerpt: So duplicates should point directly at a primary, and a primary is not itself a duplicate of anything. ... That's the rule as intended. It's not enforced.
